sourceSites.restorePush: src/forge/scenarios-v2.js:218-222: if goals include 'restore', failed = random structural node; relations.push({type:'dependsOn', from: primaryNode.id, to: failed.id}) with NO existence check
sourceSites.bypassEnumeration: src/forge/kernel.js:277-288 legalActions: one BYPASS per dependsOn relation whose target is failed, in range (1) and has a live substitute, energy >= 3; no uniqueness check

historical.why: scoreSet takes max/min utility and the first truth entry per selected id; a duplicated identical branch changes neither, so R/B/N regret, hit and catastrophe are unchanged by the duplicate entry. Whether S0/Nexus would have SELECTED differently on a 9-entry menu is not testable without deduplicating native actions (prohibited) and is not tested.

oodRolesPrimaryContrast.note: At H2 the frozen rule selects S0, so the witness row contributes exactly 0 to routed-minus-S0; excluding it changes the mean by 1.1e-4, removes one tie, and changes no catastrophe count. STRUCTURAL_OOD_CONFIRMED is unaffected.

answers.Q1_cause: Generator defect, not kernel or policy: for a restore objective scenarios-v2 appends dependsOn(primary -> failed) without checking that the topology already contains that edge. In this star world primary = hub n0 and failed = leaf n5, and the star topology already has n0 -> n5, so the relation exists twice. The kernel enumerates BYPASS once per dependsOn relation (n5 failed, in range 1, two live substitutes, energy 40), producing two identical BYPASS(n5, dependent n0) descriptors. Warm-up (WAIT-only), the symmetric surface, the public view and the decision packet each carry the list 1:1, so the menu has 10 entries and 9 distinct ids; the predecessor nativeLock assertion reproduces NATIVE_MENU_MISMATCH before any policy call.
answers.Q2_semantics: The two entries are one action listed twice: identical type, actor, target and parameters, identical id, and executing either yields the identical child world (both relation copies are removed and one dependent -> substitute edge is added). They are not two distinct actions that happen to share an id.
answers.Q3_identity: Action identity is forgeActionKey = sha256(stableStringify([actionType, actorId, target, parameters])) (key-order invariant); the public surface actionId is canonicalActionKey('R0', action) = the same key. The descriptor label actionId ('forge/bypass') is not identity. Two entries are the same action iff their ids are equal; legitimately distinct actions always differ in type, actor, target or parameters (e.g. REINFORCE vs REPAIR of one target, BYPASS with different dependents). Twin handles: D4 = key of the oriented action; IDENTITY = opaque handle, bijective on distinct originals (both copies of a duplicate receive the same opaque handle); ORDER = original handles.
answers.Q4_emptyMenus: Not observed (0/9,456) and not producible for an admitted world: the kernel always appends WAIT when a controlled actor exists and the world is non-terminal, and terminal-after-warm-up worlds are rejected earlier. The rule still covers EMPTY_MENU defensively.
answers.Q5_laterStepMenus: No later policy-facing menu exists: every Forge world in this protocol is exactly one decision; all policy-facing menus (original + 8 D4 + IDENTITY + ORDER) are built from the post-warm-up world before any policy call. Evaluator-internal continuation menus (H2 greedy steps) are not policy-facing; a duplicate there is decision-inert because the continuation replaces its incumbent only on a strictly higher rank or strictly smaller key (src/forge-symmetric/counterfactual-symmetric-v1.js:42-51), and an empty continuation menu simply ends the continuation. The rule therefore validates policy-facing menus only and never inspects evaluator internals (which would not be outcome-blind).
answers.Q6_silentAdmission: Yes. 3H.1-D/F confirm-core has no menu-uniqueness check (its only uniqueness guard is DUPLICATE_WORLD_HASH). This world was admitted and scored in 3H.1-F OOD_ROLES; its recorded truth lists the duplicated optimal id twice (tieCount 2, true 1) and the UNIFORM_RANDOM expectation counted 10 entries (hit 0.2, distinct-menu value 1/9). 3H.1-D (1,152 worlds), the 3H.1-F control and other OOD strata, and the 288 development worlds contain no malformed menu. The predecessor connector was the first component to check and it aborted rather than admitting.
answers.Q7_historicalImpact: None on any conclusion. One of 9,456 spent worlds; its routed-minus-S0 contrast is exactly 0 (H2: rule = S0); excluding it moves OOD_ROLES delta-nreg from -0.20950 to -0.20962, sign 641/27/1156 -> 641/27/1155, catastrophes 3/3 unchanged. Diagnostic fields of that one row (tie count, uniform-random expectation) were biased. Registration 0364164c produced no results, so nothing there is affected.
